item.title: Atiku embraces ‘Daddy Subsidy’ nickname, promises Nigerians relief at 80
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has embraced the nickname “Daddy Subsidy” as he marked his 80th birthday on Wednesday, promising Nigerians that relief would come and pledging to make the country affordable again. Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, made the remark in a post on X while thanking Nigerians for their birthday wishes and prayers. He said the nickname was among the names Nigerians had given him that he particularly enjoyed, adding that he remained committed to making life easier for citizens. Of all the names Nigerians have given me, "Daddy Subsidy" may be the one I enjoy most on my birthday. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon. To the sons and daughters scattered across the country: relief is coming, and it will follow the… https://t.co/LZo7x3Mgf9 — Atiku Abubakar (@atiku) November 25, 2026 “Of all the names Nigerians have given me, ‘Daddy Subsidy’ may be the one I enjoy most on my birthday. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon,” he wrote. Addressing Nigerians across the country, the former vice-president promised that relief was coming, making an apparent reference to his position on petrol subsidy and the hardship associated with its removal. “To the sons and daughters scattered across the country: relief is coming, and it will follow the barrel. I will make Nigeria affordable again,” Atiku added. Atiku’s birthday message comes amid continued political debate over the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, which has contributed to increased living and transportation costs. Meanwhile, President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Atiku on his 80th birthday, commending his contributions to Nigeria’s political development, democracy, education and the private sector. In a statement issued by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu said he shared with Atiku a commitment to democratic pluralism, political participation and allowing Nigerians to present alternative ideas on governance. The president recalled supporting Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition under the defunct Action Congress platform, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to compete and contribute to national discourse. Tinubu also praised Atiku’s investments in education and entrepreneurship, particularly the establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had contributed to expanding access to higher education and developing human capital. Despite their differences in political affiliation and views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability remained important. He wished the former vice-president good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to Nigeria and humanity as he joined the octogenarian club. item.title: ‘Despite our differences, Nigeria comes first’ – Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, noting that despite their political differences and occasional disagreements, their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability must remain paramount. Tinubu, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, commended Atiku’s contributions to Nigeria’s development, particularly his years of political engagement and commitment to democratic pluralism. The message was shared by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. Tinubu recalled that he supported Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to participate, offer alternative visions and contribute to discussions on leadership and governance. He said his political philosophy had consistently emphasised strengthening democratic institutions, respecting divergent opinions and ensuring that political competition served the interests of Nigerians. The President also reiterated his advocacy for politics without bitterness, saying room should always be left for reconciliation after disagreements among political opponents. “Despite our different political affiliations and occasional disagreements, Nigeria’s democracy must continue to benefit from citizens who remain committed to democratic engagement, national development, and the rule of law,” he said. Tinubu also commended Atiku’s contributions to education, entrepreneurship and the private sector, particularly his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had expanded access to quality higher education and strengthened human capital development. Although he acknowledged that he and Atiku now belonged to different political camps and held contrasting views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability should remain paramount. “Therefore, as the former vice president joins the Octogenarian Club, I wish him good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to the nation and humanity,” he said. “Happy 80th birthday, Your Excellency,” the President added. Atiku, who served as Nigeria’s vice president from 1999 to 2007, has contested the presidency several times and is the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate for the 2027 elections. item.title: Reps order contractor back to failed East-west road culverts
item.description: …Demand urgent repairs, four-week monitoring of project By Gift Chapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Ministry of Works to direct Rock Result Nigeria Limited to return immediately to the site and rehabilitate or reconstruct damaged box culverts along the East-West Road, particularly at Iheke in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Hon. Oboku Abonsizibe Oforji, who drew the attention of lawmakers to the reported deterioration of the culverts and the need for urgent intervention to prevent further damage and potential safety risks. The House recalled that it had, on October 3, 2023, adopted a motion on the deplorable condition of the East-West Road, particularly the Iheke axis, following which the Federal Government undertook further interventions. The interventions included the construction of box culverts, approval and release of funds for rehabilitation and flood mitigation works, payments to Rock Result Nigeria Limited and the re-award of the contract to Setraco Nigeria Limited for the continuation of the road dualisation project. However, lawmakers expressed concern over reports that the constructed box culverts had deteriorated, despite the financial commitments made by the government. They said the reported condition of the drainage infrastructure underscored the need for a technical assessment of the works, including the materials used, construction standards and supervision of the project. The House noted that the East-West Road was a major economic and social corridor connecting Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta states to other parts of the country, serving communities and facilitating the movement of people, goods and services. It warned that the deteriorating condition of the road could further disrupt transportation and expose motorists and other road users to safety risks. Lawmakers also expressed concern that the dualisation of the East-West Road from Ahoada in Rivers State through the Bayelsa axis to Patani in Delta State remained incomplete, despite earlier completion targets of April 2025 and November 2025. Consequently, the House urged the Ministry of Works to ensure that Rock Result Nigeria Limited returned to the site without delay to carry out the required rehabilitation or reconstruction of the damaged culverts in accordance with approved engineering standards. It also called for adequate technical supervision, quality assurance and an independent engineering assessment of the remedial works to reduce the risk of further structural problems. In addition, the lawmakers urged the ministry to ensure the completion of the dualisation of the Ahoada-Bayelsa and Patani sections of the road by Setraco Nigeria Limited. The House mandated its Committee on Works and Legislative Compliance to monitor the implementation of the resolutions and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. item.title: YABATECH non-teaching staff threaten indefinite strike
item.description: …Protest over unpaid allowances, give management until Thursday By Adesina Wahab Non-teaching staff of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, on Wednesday protested the non-payment of several allowances owed them, threatening to embark on an indefinite strike from Thursday if their demands were not met. The workers, under the umbrella of the Non-Teaching Staff Union of Polytechnics (NOTSUP), staged a protest march around the campus, led by the union’s Branch Chairman, Bayo Sanusi. They marched to the Administrative Block, which houses the Rector’s office, the Bursary Department and the institution’s main gate, singing solidarity songs and displaying placards bearing various messages. Addressing the protesters, Sanusi expressed displeasure over what he described as the exclusion of non-teaching staff from the payment of allowances, despite the reported payment of similar entitlements to teaching staff. He said teaching and non-teaching employees played complementary roles in the administration of tertiary institutions and should be treated fairly. “I don’t know whether our people have seen a bird flying with one wing. It is not possible. Tertiary institutions like ours have teaching and non-teaching staff and we complement one another. NOTSUP is made up of NASU and SSANIP members and we are united in calling for the payment of our dues. A labourer, they say, is worth his wages,” he said. Sanusi said the union’s national leadership had engaged the Federal Government on the outstanding allowances and reached an agreement on their payment. He added that the Minister of Education had directed the managements of federal polytechnics and colleges of education to source funds for the payments from available resources, including savings from capital expenditure and internally generated revenue, with a promise that the Federal Government would reimburse the institutions. According to him, at least three federal polytechnics had complied with the directive and paid the allowances, while non-teaching staff at YABATECH were still awaiting payment. He said the union had engaged the college management and was assured last Wednesday that the outstanding entitlements would be paid, but the promise had yet to be fulfilled. “In line with the directive by the Minister, at least three federal Polytechnics have paid. Here at YABATECH, teaching staff have been paid leaving us in the lurch like orphans. We are not less human than teaching staff. We have contacted our management here and last Wednesday, they promised to pay. A week has passed and nothing has happened,” he said. The union chairman questioned why the management had been able to pay teaching staff but had yet to settle the entitlements of non-teaching employees. He said the rising cost of living had worsened the hardship faced by workers, citing the daily transport expenses incurred by some staff members who commute from areas such as Ikorodu to the college. item.title: Reps seek clarification over mining marshals’ letter to lawmaker
item.description: …Give NSCDC seven days to submit operational records By Gift Cnapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals Development has asked the Commander of the Mining Marshals, ACC Attah John Onoja, to tender a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of a letter concerning a member of the House, Hon. Abdulmalik Danga. The committee also gave the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) seven days to submit outstanding operational records relating to petitions on the activities of the Mining Marshals, including complaints about arrests, detention of mining operators and the closure of mining sites. The decisions followed an investigative hearing chaired by Hon. Jonathan Gaza, during which lawmakers sought clarification from Onoja over a July 24, 2026 letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas. The letter concerned the intervention of Danga, who represents Adavi/Okehi Federal Constituency of Kogi State, in matters relating to the activities of the Mining Marshals. In the correspondence, Onoja expressed reservations about the lawmaker’s intervention, linking it to concerns surrounding the enforcement of regulations against illegal mining. Reading an excerpt from the letter, Gaza said the language used in the correspondence raised concerns about the manner in which a serving member of the National Assembly was addressed. The letter stated: “While we respect the rules of lawmaking in shaping the society through oversight legislative functions, we strongly view the action of Abdulmalik Danga as anti-government and motivated by illegal mining cartels whose unlawful activities are being disrupted by the sanity being restored in the mining sector.” The committee members questioned the basis for the assertions and whether the correspondence reflected an authorised institutional position of the NSCDC. Responding, Onoja told the committee that he wrote the letter in his personal capacity as Commander of the Mining Marshals and did not intend to challenge the constitutional powers of the legislature. He said: “Mr. Chairman, permit me to state clearly on record. My response, my letter, in my personal capacity as the Commander Mining Marshals, is not in any way looking into the legislative powers of the Committee. The letter is speaking to the motion as moved.” Gaza, however, questioned the explanation, particularly because the correspondence was written on NSCDC letterhead and carried an official reference number. The committee chairman consequently asked the NSCDC Commandant-General, Ahmed Abubakar Audi, to clarify whether the letter represented the official position of the Corps or was issued without institutional authorisation. Audi said the Corps had administrative procedures requiring officers to obtain approval before issuing correspondence on behalf of the Commandant-General. item.title: ₦1.45trn Lagos ports upgrade targets 20,000 jobs
item.description: …As FG flags off Apapa, Tin Can modernisation By Efe Onodjae The Federal Government on Wednesday flagged off a £746 million (about ₦1.45 trillion) modernisation of Apapa and Tin Can Island ports in Lagos, targeting 48-hour cargo clearance and the creation of 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The project is expected to reduce cargo delays, lower logistics costs and improve Nigeria’s competitiveness in global trade. Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Adegboyega Oyetola, who performed the groundbreaking at Tin Can Island Port, said the upgrade had become urgent as cargo throughput had outgrown existing port infrastructure. Oyetola said Nigeria’s cargo throughput had increased from 8.11 million metric tonnes in 1977 to 129.3 million metric tonnes, while merchandise trade had risen from $17 billion to over $100 billion annually. He said the project would involve rehabilitation of quay walls and berths, dredging of navigation channels, improved access facilities and installation of modern cargo-handling equipment. According to him, cargo dwell time at Nigerian ports had historically ranged between 10 and 18 days, compared with three to five days at leading international ports, costing the economy an estimated $4 billion annually. He said the upgrade would attract international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo and expand transshipment opportunities. Also speaking, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, described the project as Nigeria’s largest sovereign export credit transaction since 2009. He said the financing arrangement demonstrated international investor confidence in Nigeria’s economic reforms. Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, assured that the project would be delivered in line with approved designs, engineering standards and contractual timelines. item.title: Tinubu pledges to rescue abducted Borno schoolchildren
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri MAIDUGURI — President Bola Tinubu has pledged that his administration will do everything possible to secure the release of about 70 schoolchildren abducted from Mussa Primary School and Government Technical School, Lassa, in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State. Tinubu made the pledge on Wednesday in Maiduguri while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-East Zonal Rally held at the El-Kanemi Sports Centre. The President said his administration remained committed to rescuing the children abducted by suspected Boko Haram terrorists and defeating insurgency in the North-East. “We shall do everything possible to rescue the schoolchildren abducted in Mussa and Lassa communities,” he said. The abductions, which occurred in the first quarter of 2026, involved more than 30 children, including toddlers, from Mussa and over 40 students from Lassa. Tinubu also acknowledged the sacrifices of military personnel and other security operatives, particularly those serving on the frontline, assuring them of government support in the fight against terrorism. “The present administration under my leadership acknowledges the sacrifices of troops, especially those at the frontline. Therefore, government would do its best to support our security operatives to defeat terrorism in this region,” he said. On his second-term ambition, the President thanked the people of the North-East for their support for the APC-led administration, promising to consolidate on its achievements if re-elected in 2027. He described Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who hails from Borno State, as a dependable ally and commended Governor Babagana Zulum for his administration’s development efforts. Tinubu particularly cited the newly constructed International Conference Centre in Maiduguri and other projects he commissioned during his visit. Earlier, Zulum thanked the President for choosing Maiduguri as the venue for the zonal rally, expressing satisfaction with the large turnout and orderly conduct of APC supporters. He said Borno State had benefited significantly from the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda. The governor disclosed that the Federal Government had commenced construction of the Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri road, while also highlighting the establishment of the Federal Polytechnic, Monguno; Federal College of Education, Gwoza; and Federal University of Agriculture and Entrepreneurship, Bama. Zulum urged residents of Borno and other states in the North-East to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. The rally attracted seven governors from the region, including Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State. Also in attendance were the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu; wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima; former governors; ministers; members of the National Assembly and other APC stakeholders. item.title: Raheem Sterling handed 12-month suspended prison sentence for dangerous driving
item.description: Former England footballer Raheem Sterling was Wednesday given a 12-month suspended prison sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after crashing his Lamborghini. The 31-year-old was also ordered to complete 100 hours’ unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months during the sentencing hearing at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court. Sterling pleaded guilty in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on May 28, 2026. He also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen. Sterling’s sentence is suspended for 18 months. The former Manchester City forward had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes, a court previously heard. Dashcam footage released by the Crown Prosecution Service shows a black Lamborghini switching lanes multiple times before hitting a concrete barrier. Sterling won 82 England caps, the last of which came at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. The winger, currently without a club, made his senior debut at Liverpool before joining City in 2015, winning four Premier League titles. He left for Chelsea in 2022 but subsequently fell out of favour and spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal. Sterling joined Feyenoord on a short-term deal in February, playing eight times in the Eredivisie, but left at the end of the season. item.title: POLITICAL VIOLENCE: Dying for Nothing as a Nigerian Politician?
item.description: From the First Republic to the Fourth, politicians have been murdered, opposition figures silenced and political supporters killed. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. By Jide Ajani There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. On Monday, November 23, 2026, four persons were killed during an alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State. Over a dozen were said to have been injured. Mind you, in an outburst of emotive frustration about happenings inthe political sphere, the self-same Omo-Agege had used the phrase ‘ ig and die’. He was to later clarify that he was merely drawing attention to the need for credible elections. item.title: US Mission announces two-day shutdown of Abuja, Lagos offices
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The United States Mission in Nigeria has announced a two-day shutdown of its embassy in Abuja and consulate general in Lagos in observance of the country’s Thanksgiving holiday. The mission disclosed this in an announcement on its official Instagram account on Wednesday, November 25, stating that both facilities would be closed on Thursday, November 26, and Friday, November 27, 2026. The closure means that consular services and other official activities at the two diplomatic offices will be unavailable during the period. Visa applicants, travellers and members of the public with appointments or enquiries scheduled for the affected dates will be unable to access services at the facilities. The public is therefore advised to take note of the closure and plan visits accordingly, with normal operations expected to resume the following week. Thanksgiving is a federal public holiday in the United States, observed annually on the fourth Thursday of November. The holiday is traditionally marked by family gatherings and expressions of gratitude, while US diplomatic missions around the world typically suspend official operations in observance of it. item.title: Oyo 2027: APC pledges better welfare, rules out workers’ sack
item.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State has dismissed reports that its governorship candidate, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, plans to sack government workers or deny them salaries and other entitlements if elected governor in 2027. The party described the reports as a campaign of calumny allegedly orchestrated by some elements within the ruling Allied Peoples Movement (APM) to mislead the public and discredit its candidate ahead of the governorship election. Instead, the APC promised that an Alli administration would prioritise workers’ welfare through timely payment of salaries and allowances, regular promotions, improved working conditions and access to training opportunities. The party’s position was contained in a statement issued on Wednesday by its Publicity Secretary, Olawale Sadare, and made available to journalists in Ibadan. The statement followed media reports alleging that Alli would disengage a large number of government workers and deny others prompt payment of their salaries and wages if elected governor. The APC questioned the credibility of the reports, noting that they did not identify their sources, and accused some APM members of sponsoring them to undermine Alli’s governorship ambition. According to the party, the APC candidate has already outlined his plans for workers and other residents of the state in his campaign manifesto, unveiled in Ibadan a few weeks ago. “For the avoidance of doubt, Sen. Alli has explained how he would better the lot of the people of Oyo State (including government workers) in the campaign manifesto which was released in Ibadan a few weeks ago,” the statement said. The party argued that increased monthly allocations from the Federal Government had made it difficult to justify the non-payment of workers’ salaries and pensioners’ entitlements by state and local governments. It promised that, if elected, Alli would establish a new relationship between government and workers, anchored on improved welfare and recognition of their contributions to the development of the state. The APC said serving and retired civil and public servants would begin to enjoy improved conditions from May 29, 2027, when Alli is expected to assume office if elected. It listed workers in ministries, departments and agencies, public school teachers, academic and non-academic staff of tertiary institutions, and local government employees among the beneficiaries of the proposed reforms. The party also pledged workplace safety, a conducive working environment and greater involvement of workers in the formulation and implementation of policies affecting them. It further promised to end what it described as the imposition of “shylock consultants” on government workers, while providing opportunities for periodic training and retraining programmes locally and overseas. item.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
item.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures. item.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
item.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. item.title: 21% of Nigerian women aged 15-49 suffer violence — Oxfam
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — Oxfam Nigeria has raised the alarm over the prevalence of gender-based violence in the country, disclosing that more than one in five Nigerian women aged 15 to 49 have experienced physical or sexual violence. The organisation also disclosed that 23.4 per cent of women in Nigeria had experienced intimate partner violence, while the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) recorded 84,187 complaints of domestic violence in 2024. Oxfam’s Country Director in Nigeria, Tijani Ahmed Hamza, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja at a press conference to commemorate the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence and formally introduce its five-year FemFocus programme. Hamza said the figures, drawn from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey and NHRC records, highlighted the urgent need for stronger institutional responses, improved survivor support services and better access to justice. He expressed concern that despite progress in enacting laws to combat gender-based violence, implementation remained weak, with several states lacking essential facilities to support survivors. According to him, 35 states and the Federal Capital Territory have domesticated the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act or enacted equivalent legislation, but 14 states still lack Sexual Assault Referral Centres. He added that only eight states maintained consistent forensic services, while six had neither referral centres nor shelters for survivors. “Nigeria’s crisis is no longer primarily a gap in laws; it is a gap in implementation, financing and infrastructure,” he said. The Oxfam director further noted that financial constraints continued to prevent many survivors from accessing justice, with some spending as much as N100,000 out of pocket in pursuit of justice. He said the FemFocus programme was designed to address these challenges through improved survivor support services, stronger legal accountability and enhanced protection for Women Human Rights Defenders. The five-year initiative, which will run from 2026 to 2030, is supported by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands, with €6.4 million allocated to Nigeria. Hamza said the programme would focus on preventing violence against women and girls, expanding access to survivor-centred services, strengthening laws and institutional accountability, and protecting women human rights defenders. He urged federal and state governments, law enforcement agencies, the judiciary, traditional institutions, the media and the private sector to support survivors, provide funding for grassroots feminist movements and ensure accountability. Also speaking, the National Coordinator of Christian Women for Excellence, Empowerment and Development and Chairperson of the African Women Leaders Network, Prof. Fummilayo Para-Mallam, urged stakeholders to move beyond repeated awareness campaigns and adopt practical measures to address gender-based violence. item.title: Barca, Real Madrid chief fail to reach agreement over ref scandal accusations
item.description: Real Madrid and Barcelona failed to reach an agreement on Wednesday in a conciliation hearing over statements made by Los Blancos president Florentino Perez regarding the Negreira refereeing scandal, a source from the Catalan club confirmed to AFP. The hearing followed a lawsuit filed by Barcelona on June 12 against Perez for his statements in May, in which he accused the Spanish champions of scheming to obtain favourable treatment from referees. “The aim of this lawsuit is for Mr. Perez to retract certain statements he made, knowing they were false, which are defamatory and offensive to the club’s image and reputation,” Barcelona had declared when initiating legal action. “In the event that this lawsuit is not duly addressed, Barcelona will proceed to file the corresponding criminal complaint for defamation,” Barca added in June. “When someone makes statements and you might be mistaken or go too far with your words, a conciliation hearing gives you the chance to correct them,” Barca president Joan Laporta told reporters before the hearing on Wednesday. “If that opportunity is not taken, it means we see malicious intent and we will have to continue with the proceedings.” Barca could now file a criminal complaint against Perez over his remarks. The main cause of the Catalan club’s anger was the press conference on May 12 in which Perez called elections for the Real Madrid presidency, which he later won. In that appearance he reiterated his accusations against Barca regarding the matter known as the “Negreira case”. Spanish courts are investigating alleged payments of around 7.5 million euros ($8.2m) made over almost two decades by Barcelona to companies belonging to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former number two in Spain’s refereeing hierarchy. The investigation seeks to determine whether those payments may have been used to obtain any competitive advantages, something Barcelona deny, claiming they were solely for reports analysing referees. item.title: Katsina govt orders emirs to seek clearance before hosting foreign guests
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Katsina State Government has directed emirs and other traditional rulers to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors at their palaces. Commissioner for Information and Culture Bala Salisu Zango announced the directive in a statement on Wednesday, saying rulers must obtain approval from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters in the Office of the Secretary to the State Government before hosting foreign guests. “The directive is intended to ensure proper coordination, security, and adherence to official protocols during visits to Emirs’ palace by foreign nationals, while also placing the traditional rulers under a formal regulatory framework regarding international relations,” the statement said. It added that the measure was intended to “streamline interactions with foreign nationals and ensure that the government is fully aware of international engagements involving traditional institutions.” Zango said the policy was part of the state government’s broader security strategy, adding that “the state government partly relies on traditional rulers as key stakeholders in peace-building.” The directive followed the government’s suspension of the Emir of Daura, Umar Faruk Umar, from official engagements and travel, pending an investigation into an allegation made by Polish tourist Mirka Czee. The government also set up a committee to investigate the allegation and advise it on the appropriate course of action. Czee alleged that the Emir touched her breasts without her consent during a visit to his palace on November 14. She said she recorded part of the encounter using Meta smart glasses and released the video after leaving Nigeria. The Daura Emirate Council said it was reviewing the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated. The Katsina State Government said the Emir’s suspension would remain in place pending the committee’s findings, which it said would be implemented. Czee later shared screenshots of abusive messages and death threats she said she received after publishing the allegation. Amnesty International Nigeria condemned the threats, saying she had received hundreds. item.title: INEC deploys AI unit to combat misinformation ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Edwin Philip ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence (AI) division within its Information and Communication Technology department to tackle misinformation, disinformation and AI-driven manipulation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission said the growing use of generative AI, synthetic voice cloning, deepfakes and coordinated online campaigns had made information management a critical part of election security. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, stated this in a keynote address at the Nigeria Election Risk and Readiness Summit 2026 in Abuja on Wednesday. Amupitan, who was represented by his Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said elections could be influenced by false information even before voting commenced. The summit, convened by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) as part of its 2026 Media and Development Conference, had the theme, “Securing the Vote and Protecting the Frontliners.” According to the INEC chairman, fabricated audio recordings, doctored videos and false election results could trigger panic, discourage voter participation and spark communal violence. He cited an incident during the Federal Capital Territory election in which a viral video falsely claimed that members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) were being killed in parts of Abuja on election day. Amupitan said INEC worked with the NYSC to verify and debunk the claim, preventing the misinformation from causing panic or disrupting the electoral process. He said the commission was adopting a zero-tolerance approach to communication gaps but acknowledged that tackling false narratives in a highly connected society required collaboration. INEC, therefore, called for an institutionalised partnership with independent fact-checking organisations, including Dubawa, media organisations, civil society groups and the National Orientation Agency. The commission also pledged to provide verified journalists and fact-checkers with timely access to official information to enable them to counter false claims with accurate data. Addressing journalists at the summit, INEC urged freelance and newsroom reporters to complete their accreditation before the portal closes, stressing that the registration deadlines are guided by the Electoral Act and cannot be extended arbitrarily. On its preparations for the elections, the commission said it had procured about 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, replaced batteries in serviceable units and established climate-controlled storage facilities across the states. It also said it had reduced the voter-verification threshold per BVAS device from 1,250 to 850, with additional devices to be deployed to larger polling units to keep accreditation within an estimated one to two minutes.
